_source: Bible p.29 'Startvaerdier og balancering'. First implementation baseline, not claimed final balance. Change with evidence (docs/DECISIONS.md).

oxygen._note: Captain life support reserve in % (scrubbers + tank). Stasis uses a little per travel day; severe impacts leak; the workbench repairs scrubbers with components.

approach._note: Approach flight after a journey: hazards per route (data/routes). Each impact costs hull; a severe one also leaks oxygen. Evasive burns cost fuel; the NAV autopilot flies cautiously (fewer impacts) but burns more.

districts._note: District radius multiplier = 1 + colony_year / growth_years, capped at max_scale (D-032).

workforce._note: Share of adults that work as construction/staff labor (children never work).

priorities._note: R9/D-034: the year-20/40 priority is a lasting modifier set; the latest decision is the colony's course. Missing keys mean 1.0 (multipliers) or 0 (deltas). Every priority has a gain and a price.

trust_effects._note: R9/D-034: trust is a dial with systemic effects. Below 'low' adults work less and incubation demands more reserve days; above 'high' adults work more and crises cost less. Trust never decides an ending on its own.

ark_power._note: R9/D-034: after landing the Ark's core is emergency power. It burns fuel in proportion to the share of its output the colony actually draws; 'standby_burn' is the fraction of the daily burn spent while idle. The Ark 'still shields' the colony when its emergency power carries more than 'shielded_share' of demand now, or was drawn on more than 'shielded_share' of the last year's days (an 8 kW core can never carry 15% of a 300 kW grid; the epilogue's 'every night the emergency power still flows' is the measurable form). Shielded colonies are never 'independent'.
